static_traits.name: Lin Xueqing
static_traits.social_status: Social life affected by avoiding going out in winter; relationship tension with friends and family; lacking specific supporters to confide in or seek help from
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of similar problems; has not yet received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to describe pain feelings concretely; slightly nervous but positive attitude, willing to try small-step changes

basic_info.main_problem: Fear of going out arising from facial pain caused by winter cold, gradually worsening over the past year and completely avoiding going out in winter, leading to long periods indoors, isolation, and impaired socializing.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to reduce and overcome the fear of going out in winter, in order to lessen the impact on daily life and mental health.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, during winter outdoors, experienced a severe facial pain (feeling both frozen and burning); since then developed a fear of going out in winter; as each winter arrives, the fear gradually worsens, and they have begun to avoid going out entirely, leading to isolation and affecting relationships with friends and family.

core_beliefs: Going out in winter is unsafe and brings hard-to-bear pain
I am unable to bear that kind of pain

special_situations.event: When winter comes, temperatures are very low, or cold wind blows, needing to go out for daily errands (such as shopping, handling affairs)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go out in cold weather, I will again experience unbearable facial pain
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying completely indoors and canceling all outdoor activities to avoid pain
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Going out will hurt unbearably; I had better stay indoors

special_situations.event: Recalls or sees the snowy scenery outside the window, or hears others invite me to winter outdoor activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Whenever thinking of going out, negative consequences outweigh any positive experience; the positive parts are not worth considering
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring the winter fresh air and snow scenery once liked, focusing on pain memories and negative information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The parts of winter I like are meaningless, because going out will be very painful

special_situations.event: Plans whether to go out in winter to complete necessary daily errands
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If absolute painlessness cannot be guaranteed, I must never go out
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Never going out whenever there is risk, to avoid any possible discomfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Either completely safe or a disaster; cannot take risks

special_situations.event: Recalls severe facial pain experienced in cold weather a year ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The worst past experience will inevitably repeat
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses that episode of pain as the basis for judgment, filtering out other milder situations and possible coping methods
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This outing will definitely be as bad as that time

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be able to go out safely and at ease in winter too and maintain contact with others
core_conflict.fear: Fearing experiencing unbearable facial pain again and losing control, leading to collapse and intense anxiety
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of pain and anxiety by avoiding going out; staying indoors to maintain a sense of safety

object_relations.object_representation: The winter outside world experienced as a cold threatener that would hurt oneself
Friends and family are experienced as others who expect them to join socializing and outings (becoming a source of stress in the cold season)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others suggest trying small-step outings in winter (for example, first staying on the porch for a few minutes)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Going out equals experiencing unbearable pain again; believing suggestions may underestimate the risk
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a cautious, prudent tone emphasizes the necessity of 'avoiding pain', highlighting safety reasons and turning the topic back to safety strategies and preparation conditions.

manifestations: Staying indoors all winter leading to relationship tension with friends and family; lacking supporters to confide in; feeling isolated
outcomes: Impaired social life and increased sense of distance
Emotional distress and affected mental health

manifestations: Fear markedly limits autonomy in going out and participating in activities; life choices are controlled by weather and worries about pain

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Limiting outing choices with safety as the primary criterion
Narrows the range of contact to only brief stops on the porch
Frequently emphasizes in sessions that 'staying indoors is safer'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Suppressing the urge to go out and socialize, instead using self-restraint (staying home) to cope with discomfort
Avoiding seeking external support; bearing fear and discomfort alone

positive_force: Once liking winter; able to recall and identify its positive aspects (fresh air, snowy scenery)
Positive attitude and willing to try small-step changes (such as staying on the porch first)
Has the willingness for reality testing and reframing, willing to cooperate with recording and practice
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking, and mental filteringReinforcementFear
Avoidant behavior becomes entrenched and expands, leading to isolation and functional impairment
Lacks a dependable social support system and finds it hard to obtain comfort and assistance
Strong anticipatory fear of pain; tending to use the worst-case scenario as reference

target_behavior.behavior: Strong fear of and avoidance of going out in winter (staying indoors long-term)
antecedent: Cold winter weather (low temperatures, cold wind, snow)
Considering needing to go out for daily errands
When thinking of or being invited to winter outdoor activities
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic expectations of cold and anxiety associations formed after experiencing severe facial pain in the cold a year ago; worrying the pain will be unbearable
target_behavior.function: Escaping pain and anxiety; maintaining short-term security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Social and tense family relationships; declining scope and quality of life; increased sense of isolation; mental health affected
